sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
This page lists all Achievements in Escape from Tarkov and Escape from Tarkov: Arena.

When achievement requirements are fulfilled, there is a notification in the bottom right corner of the screen:

Fulfilled achievements are displayed on player profiles. They persist throughout game profile resets and Prestige, including the attached rewards, while partial achievement progress is lost.

Bug: Hidden achievements are currently not visible in the PvE game mode, but are still being awarded if the requirements are fulfilled.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
Some of the achievement names are references:
- Star Called Sun: Referencing the Russian song "Звезда по имени Солнце" ("A Star Named the Sun") from "Кино" (Kino).
- That's What She Said: With also taking the icon and description into account, this is a reference to the TV show "The Office" in which the character Michael Scott uses this phrase frequently.
- Lost: Referencing the TV show "Lost", in which a plane crashes in a jungle on an island.
- All On Red: Referring to betting everything on the color red in a roulette game. In the related questline, Skier has the player amass a lot of gear and items to equip a supposed BEAR squad to take over a well-stocked base, but his contact ultimately just disappears after receiving it.
- Highway To The Danger Zone: Referencing the song "Danger Zone" from Kenny Loggins.
- Grouse Hunting: Glukhar (Глухарь) in Russian means wood grouse.
- Deal to Make: Reshala (Решала) in Russian means "Dealmaker" or "[Problem] Solver".
- Funny Graveyard Keeper: This is a reference to the character "Mr. Jones" from the game "Mr. Jones' Graveyard Shift", whose outfit is similar to Kaban's.
- John's Heir: Referencing the media franchise and its titular character John Wick, known for his acumen with pistols.
- Chris's Heir: A reference to the celebrated United States Navy SEAL sniper Christopher Scott Kyle, whose longest confirmed kill was achieved with a single shot from 1.2 miles (1,930 meters) away, during a mission in Sadr City, eastern Baghdad, Iraq, in 2008.
- Drunken Master: Referencing the 1978 Hong Kong martial arts film starring Jackie Chan and its titular character Beggar So.
- Samsara Wheel Spins Again: A reference to the concept of Samsara in Buddhist thought, the continuous cycle of birth, death, and rebirth that beings go through, governed by the principle of karma.
- Killer7: Referencing the 2005 action-adventure game developed by Grasshopper Manufacture and Capcom and published by Capcom for the GameCube and PlayStation 2, where the player can transform into and control any of seven assassin personae.
- Here's Johnny: Referencing Jack Torrance’s iconic line from the horror film The Shining, it has been used in popular culture to make a joke about the sudden arrival of a person.
- They Fly Now: Referencing a quote said by several characters in the film Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker, the line became a popular catchphrase to express surprise when something/someone that wasn't expected to fly is able to fly now.
